---
title: "Plan Sealing and Canonical Identity"
subtitle: "When is a Plan immutable, and what is safe to share?"
toc-depth: 2
---

**Status:** `STABILIZED` numerical/runtime identity baseline. Structured
authoring alignment remains a separate `CONVERGING` target with implementation
alignment pending.

## Seal each authoring graph at its ownership boundary

`CircuitPlan` and `CompositePlan` remain editable only during their respective
authoring phases. `CompositePlan.build()` validates and permanently seals its
private graph before returning an immutable `ComponentInstance`.
`CircuitRun(plan=..., workspace=..., versioned=False)` similarly validates and
permanently seals the outer Python Plan and canonical snapshot. Calling
`add()`, `net()`, `ground()`, `expose_pin()`, `add_port()`, or another mutator
on either sealed authoring graph raises `PlanSealedError`; SCNSim does not keep
a hidden mutable copy. This paragraph describes the executable baseline:
`net()` and callable `ground()` are not the current TARGET authoring spelling.

The target [structured-authoring contract](../contracts/automatic-semantic-circuit-diagram-layout.qmd#structured-authoring-grammar)
replaces that frozen mutator vocabulary with buses, structures, N-endpoint
`link()`, and dedicated `ground_pins()`. It retains the same seal boundary:
each operation validates before atomic commit, complete validation runs at
`CompositePlan.build()`, immutable render capture, and `CircuitRun` sealing,
and every target mutator raises `PlanSealedError` after seal. A failed target
preflight preserves every previously committed ID, zero-wire equivalence,
diagnostic source path, and provenance fact; it adds no history for the
rejected attempt, leaves the proposed ID reusable, and keeps the graph editable.
Immutable render capture validates that editable graph but never seals it. This
page does not claim those TARGET bytes are implemented.

Complete validation distinguishes registration, terminal binding, and
structural use. Ordinary two-terminal native bodies must belong to exactly one
structure; a fully bound Composite occurrence or native multi-terminal body may
remain an independent peer or be used once when its schema permits. The seal
records that choice rather than inferring it from connectivity or layout.

The current Run supports any number of Refs, Specs, and ParameterSets against
its snapshot. The `CONVERGING` Parameter System target adds independently
defined refs and ordered spaces while preserving the same no-mutation rule.
Only definitions actually consumed by registered physical fields enter that
target Plan snapshot; unused definitions do not. Exact target identity belongs
to the [Parameter System Contract](../contracts/parameter-system.qmd), not this
implementation page. Composite sealing and recursive expansion are specified
separately in
[Composite Snapshots and Recursive Expansion](composite-snapshots-and-recursive-expansion.qmd).

A change to sealed topology, an authoring baseline, Ports, couplings, or a
public component schema creates a new Plan and Run. A parameter value selected
through a declared `ParameterRef` and supplied in a `ParameterSet` does not.
Notebook authors may edit their builder and rerun the same cell, rebinding the
same `plan` and `run` variable names without restarting the kernel. This is a
new pair of objects, never mutation of the earlier Run.

By default, binding a different Plan to the same workspace replaces the prior
workspace evidence after the new Plan has sealed. `versioned=True` instead
selects a Plan-specific iteration subworkspace. The exact replacement,
one-way-upgrade, and stale-handle behavior is defined in
[Workspace, Attempts, Receipts, and Artifacts](workspace-attempts-and-artifacts.qmd#iterate-topology-in-one-workspace).

## Separate three identities

| Identity | Includes | Excludes |
|---|---|---|
| Plan | canonical component schemas, topology, nodes, authored N-link IDs and unordered member sets, effective ground membership and local ownership, Ports, couplings, baselines, and catalog source identity | workspace path, display theme, diagram-only layout or visual grouping, execution history |
| Request | Plan, Ref lineage, Spec, bound ParameterSet, operation, and numerical runtime | workspace location, progress display, and attempt history |
| Evidence | request plus workspace binding, source units, runtime files, attempt, artifacts, and receipt hashes | mutable latest pointers |

Target alignment uses one normalized immutable semantic record containing the
scope hierarchy, occurrence table, physical-leaf table, final physical-endpoint
connectivity, consumed definitions, and field bindings. Recursive traversal and
flat lookup are views over that record, not competing semantic authorities.
Plan identity includes only consumed independent definitions and physical-field
bindings, while request identity includes one effective point or exact ordered
space. Unused definitions and selected values remain outside Plan identity.

Changed machine envelopes use successor `schema_version=2`; unchanged inner
scientific algorithm IDs remain intact. No old/new authoring or artifact
identity compatibility is promised. Source provenance remains separate.
Source-unit spelling and `ground_pins()` call grouping/order remain outside
semantic Plan hashing as already specified; no additional exclusion is created
here. The canonical encoder owner implements this record and envelope. They add
no public API.

That same future alignment binds scoped N-link membership, final zero-wire
equivalence, public-boundary ownership, and canonical-ground membership. A
fixed link's endpoint tuple order is nonsemantic; replacing one N-link with
several binary links is a different authored structure even when electrically
equivalent. Effective grounded-net membership and the owner-local grounding
role remain part of the Plan. Only `ground_pins()` call grouping and tuple order
are source provenance excluded from physical and diagram identity; they do not
create another ground or visual rail.

Physical values cross the computation boundary as coherent-SI magnitude,
canonical SI unit, and declared dimensionality. Source unit and authoring form
from the executed attempt remain receipt evidence. Consequently `92 * u.fF`
and `0.092 * u.pF` may share semantic computation identity; reusing that
success does not create a new receipt only to preserve the later spelling.

## Canonicalize before hashing

Python emits UTF-8 canonical JSON with deterministic object-key order and
explicit type/schema tags. It rejects NaN, infinity, pickle payloads, and
absolute machine paths. Arrays are referenced by relative artifact identity
rather than embedded as enormous JSON lists.

Catalog provenance binds the public catalog class/module and exact obtainable
distribution or source identity. Empty custom catalogs remain constructible;
source proof becomes mandatory when a factory creates a component. The four
portable provenance forms are fixed in
[Catalog and Runtime Identity](catalog-and-runtime-identity.qmd).

The workspace/Plan/request/attempt/outcome/Result/receipt envelopes, optimization
ledgers, canonical binary64 encoding, and exact hash ranges
are fixed in [Canonical Identities and Schemas](canonical-identities-and-schemas.qmd).
Hashing the containing workspace directory is not an identity protocol.
